title: Given a Scenario, Use Remote Access Technologies

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Remote-access technologies reach private networks, graphical desktops, command lines, endpoint fleets, virtual machines, screens, meetings, or files without physical presence.
sections.callout: What needs access: network, desktop, command line, management, screen, or files?

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Choose the technology that matches the needed resource and apply authentication, encryption, least privilege, patching, authorization, and session controls.

sections.title: RDP and VPN

entries.title: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)
paragraphs: Microsoft protocol for remotely using a graphical Windows desktop.

entries.title: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
paragraphs: Creates a protected connection to a private network or service; it does not itself provide desktop control.

sections.callout: Enter the network → VPN; control a Windows desktop → RDP.

sections.title: Virtual Network Computer (VNC)
paragraphs: VNC provides graphical remote screen viewing and control with a broad cross-platform association. Security depends on implementation and configuration.
sections.callout: Windows-focused GUI → RDP; cross-platform screen control → VNC.

sections.title: Secure Shell (SSH)
paragraphs: SSH provides encrypted command-line access for Linux, servers, and network devices.
sections.callout: Secure terminal → SSH; graphical Windows session → RDP.

sections.title: Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM)
paragraphs: RMM platforms monitor endpoints, deploy software and updates, perform maintenance, and receive alerts across a fleet.
sections.callout: One interactive session → remote desktop; many managed endpoints → RMM.

sections.title: Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments (SPICE)
paragraphs: SPICE provides remote display, keyboard, and mouse interaction commonly associated with virtual-machine environments.

sections.title: Windows Remote Management (WinRM)
paragraphs: WinRM enables remote Windows administration and is associated with PowerShell remoting.
sections.callout: Windows desktop → RDP; Windows administration → WinRM.

sections.title: Third-Party Tools
paragraphs: Third-party remote capabilities include screen sharing, videoconferencing, file transfer, and desktop management.

sections.title: Screen-Sharing and Videoconferencing Software
paragraphs: Screen-sharing lets support personnel see or, when authorized, interact with a user's screen. Videoconferencing combines audio, video, meetings, and optional screen sharing without necessarily taking control.

sections.title: File Transfer and Desktop Management Software
paragraphs: File-transfer tools move logs, packages, and configuration files without controlling a desktop. Desktop-management systems centrally deploy, inventory, configure, update, and administer workstations.

sections.title: Security Considerations of Each Access Method
bullets: Use strong authentication, MFA, keys, or certificates as appropriate
Avoid unnecessary exposure to untrusted networks
Obtain user authorization for screen control
End sessions, protect saved credentials, and retain required logs

table.caption: Match the need to the technology

sections.title: Objective 4.9 Exam Trap
bullets: VPN provides network access; RDP provides a Windows desktop.
RDP is graphical; SSH is command line.
RDP is Windows-focused; VNC is broadly cross-platform.
RDP interacts with a desktop; WinRM administers Windows remotely.
Remote desktop serves a session; RMM manages a fleet.
Screen sharing displays or controls a screen; file transfer moves data.
Convenience never removes authentication, encryption, least privilege, patching, or secure disconnection requirements.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: Authenticate → encrypt → limit access → patch → disconnect.
